source.title: Make Every Example Count: On Stability and Utility of Self-Influence for Learning from Noisy NLP Datasets
source.authors: Irina Bejan; Artem Sokolov; Katja Filippova

record.tranche_reason: The study removes examples ranked by self-influence and reports downstream held-out performance, a related intervention on generalization, but it does not test the memorization-defined examples or train–test gaps in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure whether the removed examples are memorized by the version 8 criterion, nor compare their removal with removing the same number of random examples. Its reported filtering and AutoCL performance results are retained as findings about example removal and held-out performance; cited prior-work results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures self-influence ranking stability and NLP performance after filtering or curriculum scheduling. It does not test any listed version. In particular, loss-based self-influence is not V8's inclusion-based probability of correct prediction, and removal is not compared with equal-sized random removal. V1 and V8 appear as background or motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that self-influence scores are stable under tested training and ABIF hyperparameter changes, but sensitive to architecture or capacity; naturally occurring outliers do not uniformly receive high scores; and bandit-based dynamic reweighting can outperform threshold filtering. That performance conclusion requires sufficient bucket granularity and training, with only insignificant gains on clean TriviaQA.
record.recipe_differences: NLP data influence scoring and self-influence-guided example filtering or curriculum scheduling; it does not train networks to fit arbitrary labels or measure the listed generalization mechanisms.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer selection affected ranking stability; model size and attention architecture affected stability; in-distribution versus out-of-distribution evaluation changed filtering outcomes; filtering percentage and AutoCL bucket granularity affected reported downstream performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-influence filtering reduces in-distribution QA performance, slightly improves Toxicity, improves NQ-to-TriviaQA and Paracrawl-to-newstest17 performance, and gives negligible Toxicity-to-Civil Comments improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The usefulness of loss-based self-influence filtering depends on dataset quality and evaluation distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Self-influence AutoCL can outperform threshold filtering with suitable bucket granularity and sufficient training; at 10k Paracrawl steps, good threshold filtering performs better. TriviaQA gains are insignificant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic sampling from self-influence buckets can improve NLP performance relative to fixed threshold filtering, depending on configuration and training duration.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper reports downstream performance rather than train–test gaps; it does not establish that self-influence identifies memorized examples under the version 8 definition. Table values are presented in flattened layouts, and the authors describe some out-of-distribution gains as negligible or some AutoCL gains as insignificant. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these performance results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Stability correlations and noise-ranking results are not included as claim rows because they measure influence-ranking stability or noise retrieval, not the claim versions' named outcomes. Table 5's flattened result mapping is uncertain; rows are limited to the apparent configurations and noted accordingly.

untested.parts: Joint natural-label generalization and random-label fitting, including chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Large-batch held-out performance penalties under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Controlled dropout addition or removal and its effect on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal ranked by inclusion-based memorization probability, compared with equal-sized random removal. Loss-based self-influence filtering does not establish this comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are assessed against the listed versions, none of which these rows measure. The important extraction error is the swapped QA training-dataset attribution in Table 4. Table 5 also contains several method and configuration mapping errors. No additional result bearing on V1–V8 is missing.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image networks.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train–test gap.
The study does not identify examples by whether their inclusion raises the chance of predicting their own label correctly, and does not compare their removal with random-example removal.
